readouts.finding:
LINE 5: IN PLACE, NOT TRUSTED.
STAY CORRECT; REGRET GOES.
readouts.why: Line 5 holds the top place but 'there is a lack of trust'; only 'perpetual Correctness' makes regret vanish, so rank alone does not gather people, what is right does. The link holds but needs the viewer to follow two clauses, so it is weaker than 22.
readouts.lineText: Nine in the Fifth: Gathering while possessing the position—no blame. There is a lack of trust. With a Sublime Beginning, perpetual Correctness, regret vanishes.
readouts.loopNote: The hook (family, bracing for arguments) is better met by line 1: 'disorder, then gathering. If one calls out, a single handful becomes laughter. Do not worry.' Option only: AT THE BASE: DISORDER, THEN\nGATHERING. A CRY TURNS TO LAUGHTER.

readouts.finding:
LINE 5: STEADY AND CORRECT,
IT CLIMBS THE STAIRS.
readouts.why: No line says 'go see someone above you' (that comes from the Judgment, 用見大人). Line 5, 'ascending the stairs', carries the hook and meaning (growing slowly, small steps piled up) almost literally, fit 8 for a lesson like 'Climb one stair at a time.'
readouts.lineText: Six in the Fifth. Correctness brings good fortune—ascending the stairs.
readouts.loopNote: Loop confirmed broken: small steps -> seeing someone senior. Line 5 (stairs) would close it with a lesson such as 'Climb one stair at a time.' Line 6 ('ascending in darkness... ceaseless effort') is a second option for 'growing slower than you want'.

readouts.finding:
LINE 3: TALK THE CHANGE OVER
THREE TIMES; THEN TRUST.
readouts.why: The calendar comes only from the Image (治曆明時); no line mentions it. Line 3 answers the hook directly: rushing brings misfortune, and 'when the call for revolution is thrice affirmed, there is trust' (fit 8 for a lesson like 'Talk a change over until it is trusted').
readouts.lineText: Nine in the Third: Advancing brings misfortune. Correctness brings danger. When the call for revolution is thrice affirmed, there is trust.
readouts.loopNote: Loop confirmed broken (trust in change -> calendar). Line 3 fixes it: hook 'a big change nobody believes in', line 'thrice affirmed, there is trust'. Line 5's tiger is trusted 'without divination', which our copy cannot say. Line 6 (leopard vs the petty person who 'changes only the face') is another option: real change vs surface change.

readouts.finding:
AT THE TOP: STILL, STEADY,
TO THE END.
readouts.why: Line 6, 'magnanimous (solid) keeping still—auspicious', is stillness held well at the end of the hexagram; its Image note says it 'ends with generosity'. It says 'stop, and stop well' plainly, better than the current structural 'NO PAIR ANSWERS', which a newcomer cannot follow.
readouts.loopNote: The body sequence (toes, calves, waist, trunk, jaws) is the hexagram's memorable picture; line 5 'keeping still at the jaws, words are well-ordered' is an option if the short leans to overthinking and speech.

readouts.finding: LINES 2 TO 5 ALL IN THEIR PLACE.
readouts.why: The lesson is the whole climb: the goose goes shore, rock, dry land, tree, hill, heights, one place at a time, and the four lines in place show that. Line 2 (the goose reaches the rock, 'eating and drinking in contentment') is the best single line but only says one step is earned, not each.
readouts.lineText: Six in the Second. The wild goose gradually advances to the large rock. Eating and drinking in contentment. Auspicious.
readouts.loopNote: Data issue: lineTexts 3 and 4 in the input hold Image commentary, not the line statements (should be 鴻漸于陸，夫征不復，婦孕不育… and 鴻漸于木，或得其桷，无咎).

readouts.finding:
LINE 4: OUT OF PLACE, SHE WAITS.
HER TIME WILL COME.
readouts.why: Line 4 is a strong line in a weak place, and its statement is 'the Marrying Maiden delays the date. The late marriage will come in its own time': wrong place, don't push, both halves of the lesson in one line.
readouts.lineText: Nine in the Fourth. The Marrying Maiden delays the date. The late marriage will come in its own time.
readouts.loopNote: Data issue: lineTexts 2 holds Image commentary; the line is 眇能視，利幽人之貞 ('The one-eyed can see. Benefit in the constancy of a secluded person').

readouts.finding:
AT THE TOP: A GREAT HOUSE,
SCREENED. NO ONE INSIDE.
readouts.why: Line 6 enlarges his house, screens his household, and 'peering through his door—silent, with no one there'; abundance shut away in the dark is the plain opposite of lighting each corner. It teaches by counterexample, so the lesson sentence must follow right after.
readouts.lineText: Top Six. He makes abundant his roof, screens his household. Peering through his door—silent, with no one there. For three years he is not seen—misfortune.
readouts.loopNote: Option: lines 2/4 'at midday he sees the Dipper' (a screen so thick it is dark at noon) also fit 'at your fullest'.

readouts.finding:
AT THE TOP: BENT UNDER THE BED,
HE LOSES HIS AXE.
readouts.why: Line 6, 'compliant beneath the bed. Loses the resources and the axe', shows bending too far: Wang Bi says the axe is 'that by which one cuts decisively'. It carries 'bend only to what is right' by counterexample.
readouts.lineText: Top Nine: Compliant beneath the bed. Loses the resources and the axe. Correctness brings misfortune.
readouts.loopNote: Loop confirmed weak (repeat a message -> choosing what to bend to). Line 5 'no beginning, but there is an end' fits the hook 'said it once, nothing changed' and would close the loop with a lesson like 'No good start? Keep on to the end.' (Its 'three days before geng' needs explaining; leave it out.)

readouts.finding:
LINE 5: THE KING CALLS OUT,
AND STAYS WHERE HE IS.
readouts.why: Line 5, 'one sweats forth the great proclamation... the king dwells here', is one figure who calls the scattered people and holds his place so they have somewhere to return. That is 'bring them back to the centre' without the word centre.
readouts.lineText: Nine in the Fifth. In Dispersion, one sweats forth the great proclamation. In Dispersion, the king dwells here—no blame.
readouts.loopNote: Option: line 4 'dispersing the group (the faction)... there are hills', breaking up cliques so a larger whole gathers, suits 'people drifting apart' too.

readouts.finding:
LINE 3: NO LIMIT SET,
THEN SIGHING.
readouts.why: Line 3, 'if one does not regulate, then one will lament', is the hook 'saying yes to everything' and its cost; Wang Bi: 'brought about by oneself; there is no one else to blame'. A lake with no limit overflows.
readouts.lineText: Six in the Third. If one does not regulate, then one will lament. No blame.
readouts.loopNote: Option: lines 5 and 6 ('sweet regulation' vs 'bitter regulation') carry the meaning card 'Firm, but not bitter' as one point: LINE 5: SWEET LIMITS.\nAT THE TOP: BITTER LIMITS.

readouts.finding:
AT THE BASE: THE FOX
WETS ITS TAIL.
readouts.why: Line 1, 'wets its tail. Regret', is the Judgment's fox image (小狐汔濟，濡其尾) in the line itself, so the lesson 'the fox gets wet' is shown almost literally. The line does not say 'fox'; the Judgment does, so adding 'THE FOX' borrows one word from the Judgment.
readouts.lineText: Initial Six. Wets its tail. Regret.
readouts.loopNote: Placement caveat: line 1 is at the start, while the lesson says 'almost across'. Option for 'so close to done': line 3 'not yet across. To advance brings misfortune' (LINE 3: NOT YET ACROSS.\nPUSHING ON NOW GOES BADLY.). Line 6 'wets its head' comes from drinking, a different point.
